## What
One llmlint rule refuses this branch. Clear it, then prove the whole gate.

```
FAIL comments_earn_their_place
  crates/onevcs/src/sweep.rs:492: This private type comment only restates that
    `Examined` records an examined family.
  crates/onevcs/src/sweep.rs:503: This private type comment merely expands the
    self-explanatory `Skipped { path, reason }` declaration.
  crates/onevcs/src/sweep.rs:509: This private type comment restates the meaning
    already explicit in `Reclaimed { path, bytes }`.
  crates/onevcs/src/sweep.rs:515: This private type comment restates the meaning
    already explicit in `Retained { path, why }`.
```

All four are the same thing: a comment above a private variant that says what the
variant's own name and fields already say. Cut them. If any one of them carries a fact
that exists nowhere else — a unit, an invariant, a reason the variant exists at all —
keep that fact and drop the restatement around it.

Then run **`just gate`** to completion and report the result. That is the part that
actually matters here: the previous dispatch on this branch was killed by a provider
quota refusal partway through its closeout, so this branch has never had a completed
gate run. Do not assume the rest is green because it was green earlier.

## Why
This branch is 101 commits and has been published, superseded, and republished twice
tonight; it is currently blocked from merging. Its subject is a `sweep` verb that must
never claim more than it proved, and the review bar it is being held to is the same
one: a comment that restates its declaration is a line that claims to inform and does
not.

The reason a manager is dispatching four comment deletions rather than doing them is
that the gate is the thing being bought here, not the deletions. A completed
`just gate` on this exact tree is the missing evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
- The four sites named above no longer carry a comment that restates the declaration,
  and any nowhere-else fact among them is kept. Say what you kept and why.
- `just lint-llm-diff origin/main` reports no findings. Report the run id.
- `just gate` runs to completion and is green. Report it. If it fails on something
  other than these comments, report exactly what — do not widen the change to chase it
  without saying so.
- No `ignore` directive is added, `llmlint.yml` is not edited, and no `cargo deny`
  exception is added.
- Nothing else changes. The 101 commits on this branch are finished work; do not
  revise, revert, reformat, or rebase them.

Done. Tree clean, one commit: `780bb7e`, four deleted lines in `crates/onevcs/src/sweep.rs`, nothing else.

## The four comments

All four were pure restatement, so all four are gone. I kept nothing, and here is the check I did before deciding that — the only one of the four carrying a candidate fact was `Reclaimed`'s *"or that a rehearsal would have removed"*, which is a genuine invariant (a dry run records a `Reclaimed` it never removed). It is not nowhere else: it is stated at the `if report.dry_run` branch that pushes the entry (`sweep.rs:398`), on `Report::bytes` ("or would have"), and in the report's own `"would reclaim"` verb. `Skipped`'s "under the workspaces root" was the other candidate, and it is not even accurate for every case — one construction site pushes the workspaces root itself, not a directory under it. The field docs on `Examined.roots` and `Examined.unreadable` were not flagged and are untouched.

## Gate result

`just gate` ran to completion and is **green** — llmlint run `20260820T073220Z-8ab00`, 31 rules: 21 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped, 2 not relevant.

`just lint-llm-diff origin/main` on its own: no findings, run `20260820T072753Z-988a3`.

## What you need to know before you trust that green

I ran the llmlint tier four times on this identical tree. Three were green; **one was red**, and it failed the gate:

```
FAIL changed_behavior_has_e2e
  crates/onevcs/src/branch.rs:200-214: the run-root lease-acquisition failure and its
    Invalid diagnostic are not exercised by an end-to-end test.
FAIL e2e_not_mocked
  crates/onevcs/tests/e2e/refusing_fs.rs:95: mounts the custom Refusing filesystem as a
    test double instead of a naturally provisioned filesystem boundary.
```

That was run `20260820T072937Z-bb091`, between two green runs, on the same commit. The flip is in **relevance**, not verdict: the two rules that read "not relevant" in every green run are exactly the two that fail when the judge deems them relevant. So this is not noise that averages out — it is roughly a 1-in-4 chance that `gate` and the required `llmlint` CI check go red on this branch, on two sites that have nothing to do with my four deletions.

I did not chase either one. Both are pre-existing work from the 101 commits, and clearing them would need an `ignore` directive, which the criteria forbid. On the merits, for whoever picks this up:

- **`branch.rs:200-214`** is the weaker of the two. It carries a written argument that no journey can build the failure (nothing else can hold a lease on a name carrying `ids::unique()`, so a refusal means something other than onevcs is writing the state root) — but as prose, not as a suppression the rule recognises. Sibling sites in `sweep.rs` make the same argument with a real `llmlint: ignore[changed_behavior_has_e2e]` directive and pass.
- **`refusing_fs.rs:95`** looks like a misread to me. `fuser::spawn_mount` mounts a real filesystem the kernel serves; the CLI under test makes real syscalls against a real mount point. It is purpose-built, but it is not a mock of the layer under test — it is how you make `remove_dir_all` actually return EPERM. I would push back on that finding rather than suppress it.

Two follow-ups outside my subtask, for you to route: the nondeterminism above is worth a decision either way, and separately `branch.rs:203` has a mangled error string — `"a run root this                  command just cut"` — a run of spaces inside the message an operator would see.
